newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong lowers hurdle in bid for Domco.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong lowers hurdle in bid for Domco.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc on Wednesday lowered a key hurdle to its hostile bid for Domco Inc, but the move could draw out the process of a complete takeover, an Armstrong spokesman said.

To overcome the opposition of Domco's 57.1 percent equity owner, Sommer Allibert, Armstrong cut the minimum percentage of Domco stock required to be tendered to 51 percent of the shares on a fully diluted basis, from 66-2/3 percent. Armstrong is offering to buy the shares at C$23 each.
Armstrong also extended its tender offer to August 15 from July 14.

With 51 percent shareholder approval, Armstrong would be able to "consolidate the two companies for accounting purposes, but more importantly, it allows you to control the election of the (Domco) board," the spokesman said. The board control would then have to be exerted to affect the evenutal takeover, the spokesman said.
By contrast, at 66-2/3 percent, "you can do a going-private transaction, cash out the minority (shareholders) and take the company private," he said.

Three weeks ago, Armstrong announced its C$488 million bid for Domco, a deal that seeks to derail Sommer Allibert's plan to merge its floor-covering business, which includes Domco, with Germany's Tarkett AG.
"We have taken direct action today to emphasize the options available to the Domco board of directors," George Lorch, Armstrong chairman and chief executive officer, said in a press release.

"We note that the Domco board has the power ... to issue without shareholder approval a sufficient number of new shares to Armstrong such that when added to shares we purchase in our offer would enable us to obtain at least 51 percent of the shares of Domco. This would assure that Domco securityholders can receive the C$23 we offer, even if by Sommer Allibert ... continues to reject our offer," he said.
Armstrong shares fell one to 73-1/2 on Wednesday. In Toronto, Domco rose 1.50 to 20.
